correctness.rationale: Reconstructed matching conditions at two imaginary potential impurities: t=1/[(1+X)(1+Y)-XY exp(2ikd)], r=[-X(1+Y)-Y(1-X)exp(2ikd)]/denominator. With k=pi/2 and d even the phase is +1 and absorption collapses to 2b/(1+b)^2. For odd d phase -1, transmission denominator D=1+b+2x(b-x)>0 and reflection numerator R=b-2(b+1)x+2x^2, yielding A=1-(1+R^2)/D^2; transmission remains nonzero for every finite b. Differentiating gives A_prime=8P_b(x)/D^3. Under z=x/(b-x) the quartic has negative coefficients for z^4,z^3,z^2, an arbitrary z coefficient and positive constant, so Descartes plus endpoint signs gives exactly one positive root. It strictly increases then decreases and the interior maximizer beats both endpoint splits. The phase-dependence inequality is positive for every split in the interior, so odd optimum strictly outperforms even constant baseline. Substituting asymptotic series into the unique polynomial root yields x*=b/2-b^2/8+O(b^3) near zero, x*=1/2-1/(4b)+1/(4b^2)+O(b^-3) large, with deficit 1/(4b^2)+O(b^-3). Independently verified symbolic quartic derivative and z-conjugacy and eight positive-budget uniqueness cases. Numerical tests are corroboration, not all-budget proof.

value.rationale: A fixed total imaginary onsite loss is a natural resource constraint in two-port wave scattering. Even/odd site separation produces a structural parity switch, while all-budget uniqueness solves a nonconvex allocation problem globally and shows that a two-site arrangement overcomes strong-loss reflection of a single defect. The exact near-perfect scaling and upstream design limit have specific physical and mathematical meaning, while generic near-perfect one-sided absorption is explicitly acknowledged as prior.

final_claim: At k=pi/2 on the infinite nearest-neighbor chain with two lossy on-site impurities separated by d>=1 and fixed total loss gamma_L+gamma_R=2b>0: even d gives constant absorption 2b/(1+b)^2 for all splits; odd d has an exact rational absorption profile with a unique interior global optimum for every b>0, which tends to near-perfect absorption with 1/(4b^2) deficit while the optimal upstream loss tends to gamma_L=1.
limitations: At one band-centre momentum only, ideal infinite uniform lattice with imaginary onsite losses and a sum-of-loss-magnitudes budget, not a finite device or robust band absorption.
